description: The Altium Designer shell around the editors: project creation and compilation, the panels that drive navigation and editing, preferences, version control and the Altium 365 workspace, component sourcing and library management, design reuse, variants, importers and exporters, and the documentation and release infrastructure.

tools.name: Projects panel
tools.description: The tree of the open design workspace: projects, their source documents (schematics, PCB, libraries, OutJobs, Draftsman), generated files, settings and any linked Workspace items. It is where documents are added and removed, where the right-click menu exposes Compile, Validate, Project Options, Version Control and Show Differences, and where the compiled hierarchy is browsed after a build.
tools.usage: View > Panels > Projects (normally docked left); right-click the project name for project-level commands
tools.example: Right-click board.PrjPcb > Add Existing to Project… > select power.SchDoc; right-click again > Validate PCB Project board.PrjPcb.

tools.name: New Project
tools.description: Creates a project and decides where it lives. The Create Project dialog chooses the project type (PCB Project, Integrated Library, Script Project, Multi-board, Draftsman), the location — local folder or a connected Altium 365 Workspace — and optionally a project template that pre-loads sheet templates, output jobs and default rules.
tools.usage: File > New > Project…; choose type, Workspace/local location, name and folder

parameters.name: Project Type
parameters.description: PCB Project (.PrjPcb), Integrated Library (.LibPkg), Script Project (.PrjScr), Multi-board Project (.PrjMbd), Draftsman.

parameters.name: Location
parameters.description: Local hard disk or an Altium 365 Workspace (which adds managed version control and sharing).

parameters.name: Project Template
parameters.description: Company starting point carrying templates, rules and OutJobs.

tools.example: File > New > Project > PCB Project > Workspace 'CompanyWS' > name 'sensor_board' > Create.

tools.name: Add / Remove documents
tools.description: Manages project membership. A document only belongs to a project when it is listed in the .PrjPcb; a schematic that is merely open is a 'free document' and is ignored by compilation, ECOs and outputs — the classic reason changes do not reach the PCB.
tools.usage: Right-click the project > Add New to Project > … / Add Existing to Project…; Remove from Project to detach
tools.example: Right-click sensor_board.PrjPcb > Add New to Project > Schematic; then File > Save As to name it analog.SchDoc.
tools.notes: Free documents appear under a separate 'Free Documents' node in the Projects panel.

tools.name: Compile / Validate Project
tools.description: Builds the unified data model: it links sheet symbols to child sheets, resolves ports and net labels into nets, applies parameters and directives, checks the design against the Error Reporting and Connection Matrix settings, and populates the Navigator and Messages panels. Nothing downstream — ECO to PCB, BOM, netlist, simulation — is valid until the project validates cleanly.
tools.usage: Project > Validate PCB Project <name> (earlier releases: Project > Compile)
tools.example: Project > Validate PCB Project sensor_board.PrjPcb, then read the Messages panel and double-click each error to jump to it.
tools.notes: Validation errors are classified by the Error Reporting page of Project Options; a rule set to 'No Report' silently hides real problems.

tools.name: Project Options
tools.description: The per-project settings dialog. Error Reporting sets the severity of every possible violation; Connection Matrix defines which pin-type-to-pin-type connections are legal; Class Generation controls which net and component classes are automatically created for the PCB; Comparator decides what differences are reported and which become ECOs; ECO Generation decides which changes are actually applied; Options sets output paths, netlist options and the 'net identifier scope' that governs how sheets connect.
tools.usage: Project > Project Options… (tabs: Error Reporting, Connection Matrix, Class Generation, Comparator, ECO Generation, Options, Multi-Channel, Default Prints, Search Paths, Parameters, Device Sheets, Managed OutputJobs)

parameters.name: Net Identifier Scope
parameters.description: Automatic, Flat (net labels and ports global), Hierarchical (ports only), Strict Hierarchical, or Global. Wrong scope is the usual cause of 'my nets are not connecting between sheets'.

parameters.name: Connection Matrix
parameters.description: Grid of pin electrical types deciding Error/Warning/Fatal/No Report for each combination, e.g. output-to-output.

parameters.name: Class Generation
parameters.description: Auto-create net classes from buses, component classes from rooms/sheets, and rooms per sheet.

parameters.name: Comparator / ECO Generation
parameters.description: Which differences are detected and which are turned into change orders when updating the PCB.

tools.example: Project > Project Options > Options tab > Net Identifier Scope: 'Hierarchical (Sheet entry <-> Port connections)' for a proper hierarchical design.

tools.name: Messages panel
tools.description: The output of compilation, DRC, ECO application, output generation and scripts. Each row carries a class, a severity, a document and a message, and double-clicking jumps to the offending object. Keeping it visible during validation is the fastest way to work through a design's errors.
tools.usage: View > Panels > Messages (opens automatically when a process produces errors)
tools.example: After Validate, double-click 'Duplicate Net Names Wire GND' to select the offending wire on the schematic.

tools.name: Navigator panel
tools.description: The compiled view of a project: the sheet hierarchy, the flattened net list, the components and the pins of whatever is selected, with cross-probing to both schematic and PCB. It answers 'where else does this net go?' across a multi-sheet design better than any search.
tools.usage: View > Panels > Navigator (requires a validated project)
tools.example: Validate the project, click net VBUS in the Navigator's Net/Bus list — every connected pin is listed and highlighted on the sheets.

tools.name: Properties panel
tools.description: The context-sensitive editor for whatever is selected or whatever placement command is active. With nothing selected it shows the document's own properties (grids, units, sheet size, layer visibility); with objects selected it edits their common properties; during a placement command it edits the object about to be placed. It replaced most of the old modal dialogs.
tools.usage: View > Panels > Properties (F11 toggles in many configurations); or press Tab during a placement command
tools.example: Start Place > Track, press Tab, set the width and layer in the Properties panel, press Enter and continue routing.

tools.name: Preferences
tools.description: The application-wide settings tree: System (general, view, file types, installation, account), Data Management (libraries, template locations, design repositories), Schematic (general, graphical editing, compiler, grids, defaults), PCB Editor (general, display, interactive routing, defaults, layer colours, DRC), Text Editors, Scripting System, Draftsman, CAM Editor and Simulation. Preferences can be exported and imported to standardise a team.
tools.usage: File > Preferences… (also the gear icon top right)
tools.example: File > Preferences > PCB Editor > Interactive Routing > Routing Conflict Resolution: enable 'Push Obstacle' and 'Walkaround Obstacle', set Loop Removal on.
tools.notes: Use the Import/Export buttons at the bottom of the dialog to move a tuned configuration to another machine or colleague.

tools.name: Version control (Git / SVN)
tools.description: Built-in integration with Git and Subversion for locally stored projects: commit, update, revert, view history and compare revisions directly from the Projects panel and the Storage Manager. Managed projects in an Altium 365 Workspace use the Workspace's own Git-backed storage instead, with the same commit/history commands surfaced in the UI.
tools.usage: Project > Version Control > Commit / Update / Show Differences; configure in Preferences > Data Management > Version Control
tools.example: Right-click the project > Version Control > Commit Whole Project… > enter a message > Commit; then Show Differences to compare with the previous revision.
tools.notes: Binary Altium documents cannot be text-merged; treat version control as revision history and locking, not as a merge tool.

tools.name: Storage Manager panel
tools.description: Shows every file in the project folder with its version-control status and local history, and offers per-file commit, revert, diff and 'save a local revision' actions. It is the place to see exactly which files have changed since the last commit, including the generated outputs that often should not be committed.
tools.usage: View > Panels > Storage Manager
tools.example: Storage Manager > select board.PcbDoc > right-click > Compare To > Latest Version to see the graphical diff.

tools.name: Altium 365 Workspace
tools.description: The cloud workspace that hosts managed components, projects, libraries, templates and releases. It provides shared component libraries with lifecycle states and where-used data, project sharing and permissions, commenting and design reviews, the Web Viewer for stakeholders without Altium, and the manufacturing portal that publishes a released package. Sign in from the account control in the top right.
tools.usage: Sign in to the Workspace from the account button; browse with the Explorer and Components panels; File > New > Project > Location: Workspace
tools.example: Sign in to CompanyWS, File > Open Project > Workspace > sensor_board, work locally, then Project > Project Releaser to publish a release.
tools.notes: Managed components are read-only locally: they are edited in the Workspace and re-released, which is the point of the model.

tools.name: Components panel
tools.description: The unified browser over every component source: file-based libraries, database libraries, installed integrated libraries and the connected Workspace. It searches by name, parameter and supplier data, previews the symbol, footprint and 3D model, and places the chosen part onto the active schematic or PCB.
tools.usage: View > Panels > Components; drag a part onto the sheet or right-click > Place
tools.example: Components panel > select library 'Miscellaneous Devices.IntLib' > search 'Res3' > drag onto the schematic.
tools.notes: The library set shown here is configured in the panel's own menu (File-based Libraries Preferences) and under Preferences > Data Management.

tools.name: Manufacturer Part Search panel
tools.description: Searches live supplier and manufacturer catalogues (Octopart-backed aggregation) for real parts with pricing, stock, lifecycle and datasheets, and can acquire the symbol, footprint and 3D model for a chosen part directly into a library or a Workspace component. It closes the gap between 'I need a 1 A buck regulator' and a placeable, purchasable component.
tools.usage: View > Panels > Manufacturer Part Search; search, then right-click a result > Place / Acquire
tools.example: Search 'TPS62840', open the part, check stock and lifecycle, right-click > Acquire to create a Workspace component with symbol and footprint.

tools.name: Explorer panel
tools.description: The browser over a connected Altium 365 / Enterprise Server workspace: managed components and their revisions and lifecycle states, projects, templates, models and released items, with where-used and history views. It is the front end to everything the Workspace holds.
tools.usage: View > Panels > Explorer (requires a signed-in Workspace)
tools.example: Explorer > Components > Capacitors > select the 100n 0402 item > History tab to see every revision and which designs use it.

tools.name: Library management (file-based, integrated, database)
tools.description: Altium supports several library models: loose .SchLib/.PcbLib pairs, compiled .IntLib integrated libraries built from a .LibPkg library package, database libraries (.DbLib) that place parts from a company SQL/ODBC database, .DBLink files that attach database parameters to already-placed parts, and managed Workspace components. The Available File-based Libraries dialog controls which are installed, which are project-specific and which folders are searched.
tools.usage: Components panel menu > File-based Libraries Preferences… (tabs: Project, Installed, Search Path); Project > Compile Integrated Library for a .LibPkg

parameters.name: Installed
parameters.description: Libraries available to every project on this machine.

parameters.name: Project
parameters.description: Libraries added to this project only, which travel with it.

parameters.name: Search Path
parameters.description: Folders scanned for libraries and models, used to resolve footprint links.

tools.example: Build an integrated library: create a .LibPkg, add company.SchLib and company.PcbLib, Project > Compile Integrated Library — company.IntLib appears in the project outputs folder.
tools.notes: Integrated libraries cannot be edited directly; use File > Open on the .IntLib and choose Extract Sources, edit, then recompile.

tools.name: Footprint Manager
tools.description: A design-wide view of every component's footprint links: which footprint each part uses, which alternatives are attached, and whether the link resolves. It edits, adds, removes and re-validates footprint associations in bulk, which is the practical fix for a design full of 'Footprint Not Found' errors.
tools.usage: Tools > Footprint Manager… (schematic editor)
tools.example: Tools > Footprint Manager > filter by 'Not Found' > select the affected parts > Edit > point at the correct PcbLib footprint > Accept Changes (Create ECO).

tools.name: Parameter Manager
tools.description: A spreadsheet of every parameter on every object in the project — components, sheets, the project itself, pins, ports and nets — for bulk viewing, adding, renaming and editing. It is how a manufacturer part number, a tolerance column or a DNI flag is applied across hundreds of components in one operation.
tools.usage: Tools > Parameter Manager… (schematic editor); choose which object classes to include, then edit the grid
tools.example: Tools > Parameter Manager > include Parts > add column 'MPN' > paste the values from a spreadsheet > Accept Changes (Create ECO).
tools.notes: Edits are applied through an ECO, so the change list can be reviewed and reverted before it is committed.

tools.name: Variant Manager
tools.description: Defines assembly variants of a single design. Per variant, each component can be Fitted, Not Fitted or Alternate Part (a different part number with its own parameters), and the variant is carried into the schematic display, the BOM, the assembly drawings and the PCB assembly outputs. One project therefore covers every product SKU.
tools.usage: Project > Variants… (Project > Assembly Variants in some releases)

parameters.name: Fitted / Not Fitted
parameters.description: Whether the component is assembled in this variant.

parameters.name: Alternate Part
parameters.description: A different component (and its parameters) substituted for this variant.

parameters.name: Variation of parameters
parameters.description: Per-variant parameter overrides, e.g. a different resistor value.

tools.example: Project > Variants > Add Variant '12V' > set R7 Not Fitted and change U2 to the 12 V regulator part > OK; the BOM and assembly drawing now have a 12V column.
tools.notes: Enable 'Show Variations' in the schematic view options to see the crossed-out not-fitted parts while working.

tools.name: Snippets
tools.description: Reusable fragments of schematic, PCB or code saved into a snippets folder and dropped into any design later. A snippet keeps both the schematic circuit and its matching PCB placement and routing when captured from both domains, which makes it the lightest form of design reuse for things like a standard power inlet or USB-C front end.
tools.usage: Select objects > right-click > Snippets > Create Snippet from selected objects…; place from View > Panels > Snippets
tools.example: Select the USB-C connector circuit on the schematic, create a snippet 'USBC_5V', then in the next project drag it from the Snippets panel onto a sheet.

tools.name: Device Sheets
tools.description: Read-only, centrally managed schematic sheets stored in a shared folder and referenced by projects rather than copied into them. Every design that uses a device sheet gets the same, approved circuit, and updating the master sheet updates all users. Use it for standardised blocks like a processor core or a regulated supply that must not diverge between products.
tools.usage: Preferences > Data Management > Device Sheets (folder configuration); place with Place > Sheet Symbol then link to the device sheet
tools.example: Configure the device sheet folder, then in the design place a sheet symbol and choose the managed 'IMX8_CORE' device sheet as its child.
tools.notes: Device sheets are read-only in the consuming project by design; changes must be made in the master and republished.

tools.name: Multi-board projects
tools.description: Designs a system of interconnected boards. A multi-board schematic (.MbsDoc inside a .PrjMbd) shows each PCB project as a module with its connectors, and the multi-board assembly (.MbaDoc) places the real 3D boards, cables and enclosure parts to verify fit, connector mating and clearance. Connectivity is checked across the whole system, catching pin-swap errors between boards.
tools.usage: File > New > Project > Multi-board Project; add multi-board schematic and assembly documents; Design > Import from Sub-Projects
tools.example: Create the .PrjMbd, place modules for main.PrjPcb and io.PrjPcb, link their connectors, then in the assembly document position the two boards and check the ribbon cable reach.

tools.name: Harness design (Signal Harness)
tools.description: Bundles wires and buses into a single named harness so that a multi-conductor interconnect is drawn as one line. Harness Connectors define which signals a harness carries, Harness Entries attach the members, and the harness definition is stored in a .Harness file generated for the project. It keeps cable-heavy designs readable and its nets fully traceable.
tools.usage: Place > Harness > Harness Connector / Harness Entry / Signal Harness
tools.example: Place a Harness Connector named 'MotorCable' with entries PWM, DIR, FAULT, GND; draw a Signal Harness from it to the motor-driver sheet symbol.

tools.name: Signal Harness definition file
tools.description: Harness definitions generated for a project are stored in a .Harness file listing each harness type and the signals and sub-harnesses it carries. Harness connectors on the schematic reference these definitions, and the compiler expands a harness into its member nets when building connectivity.
tools.usage: Generated automatically from placed Harness Connectors; visible in the project's Generated folder
tools.example: After placing a Harness Connector 'MotorCable' with entries PWM/DIR/FAULT, the project's .Harness file records the definition for reuse on other sheets.

tools.name: Import Wizard
tools.description: Translates designs and libraries from other EDA tools into Altium projects. Supported sources include Autodesk EAGLE, KiCad, OrCAD (Capture designs and libraries, and Allegro PCB via the extracta-based path), PADS (Logic and Layout, ASCII), Mentor/Siemens Xpedition and Board Station, P-CAD, Protel 99SE, CADSTAR, CircuitStudio and Altium's own older formats. The wizard maps layers, rules and library paths and reports what could not be translated.
tools.usage: File > Import Wizard…; choose the source file type and follow the mapping pages

parameters.name: File type
parameters.description: Which foreign format to import; each has its own mapping pages.

parameters.name: Layer mapping
parameters.description: Source layer to Altium layer correspondence, critical for mechanical and documentation layers.

parameters.name: Rule import
parameters.description: Whether to translate the source tool's constraints into Altium design rules.

tools.example: File > Import Wizard > 'Allegro Design Files' > point at the .brd (Extracta must be on the PATH) > map layers > Import; review the generated report.
tools.notes: Binary Allegro .brd and .dra files must be translated to ASCII by Cadence's extracta utility, which the importer invokes — extracta.exe must be reachable on the system PATH.

tools.name: Draftsman documents
tools.description: Live, intelligent fabrication and assembly drawings. A Draftsman document places board views, section views, detail views, drill tables, layer-stack legends, BOM tables, notes and dimensions that are linked to the PCB, so the drawing updates when the board changes instead of being re-exported. It replaces exporting DXF and dimensioning in a mechanical CAD package.
tools.usage: File > New > Draftsman Document (added to the project); Place > Board Assembly View / Board Fabrication View / Drill Table / Layer Stack Legend / Note / Dimension
tools.example: New Draftsman document > Place > Board Fabrication View > Place > Drill Table > Place > Layer Stack Legend > add Notes > include the document as a Documentation output in the OutJob.

tools.name: Report Project Hierarchy
tools.description: Generates a text report of the project's compiled sheet hierarchy showing each sheet, its children and the repeat counts of multi-channel sheets. It is the quickest way to confirm that a hierarchical design compiled into the structure you intended, and it is also available as a Report output inside an OutJob.
tools.usage: Reports > Report Project Hierarchy (schematic editor, project validated)
tools.example: Validate the project, then Reports > Report Project Hierarchy — the .REP file lists top.SchDoc and its child sheets with repeat counts.

tools.name: Design Reuse via project templates
tools.description: Project templates capture an entire starting point: sheet templates and title blocks, default design rules, layer stack, OutJob configurations and folder structure. Creating a project from a template means every new design starts compliant with company standards instead of being retro-fitted.
tools.usage: Preferences > Data Management > Templates (locations); File > New > Project > Project Template
tools.example: Save a fully configured project as a template in the Workspace, then File > New > Project > choose template '4-layer standard' for every new board.

tools.name: Differences / Show Differences
tools.description: Compares two documents, two projects or a document against a version-control revision, and lists every structural difference — added, removed and changed objects, nets, components and rules. Differences can optionally be turned into an ECO so one document is updated to match the other, which is how a stray manual PCB edit is reconciled with the schematic.
tools.usage: Project > Show Differences…; choose the two sides (documents, projects, or a VCS revision)
tools.example: Project > Show Differences > 'Advanced Mode' > compare board.PcbDoc with the committed revision > review the change list.

tools.name: Engineering Change Order (ECO) dialog
tools.description: The review gate for every cross-domain change. Whether triggered by Design > Update PCB Document, Import Changes from PCB, Footprint Manager, Parameter Manager or Annotation, the change list is shown with per-change enable checkboxes; Validate Changes checks that each is legal and Execute Changes applies them, writing a change report. Nothing is modified until Execute is pressed.
tools.usage: Appears automatically from Design > Update…; buttons: Validate Changes, Execute Changes, Report Changes
tools.example: Design > Update PCB Document board.PcbDoc > Validate Changes (green ticks) > Execute Changes > Close; the PCB now matches the schematic.
tools.notes: Which differences become changes is governed by Project Options > Comparator and ECO Generation — if an expected change is missing, look there first.

tools.name: Project Releaser
tools.description: Packages a validated design into an immutable, versioned release in the Altium 365 Workspace: it validates the project, generates the configured output jobs, stores the manufacturing package with the source snapshot, and assigns a revision and lifecycle state. Downstream consumers (manufacturing portal, procurement, the Web Viewer) then reference the release rather than a folder of files.
tools.usage: Project > Project Releaser… (requires a connected Workspace and configured OutJobs)
tools.example: Project > Project Releaser > select the Assembly and Fabrication OutJobs > Prepare > review the generated data > Release to the Workspace.
tools.notes: The releaser runs project validation and DRC as part of the flow, so it will refuse to release a design with unresolved errors unless they are explicitly accepted.

tools.name: Design Reviews and Comments
tools.description: Threaded comments anchored to a point, an area or an object on a schematic or PCB, visible to everyone with access through Altium Designer, the Web Viewer or Altium 365. A Design Review collects comments into a formal review with participants and a resolution state, so feedback is tracked against the design instead of living in email.
tools.usage: View > Panels > Comments; the comment toolbar button to add one; reviews are created from the Workspace project page
tools.example: Click Add Comment, drag a region around the connector, type 'Check keep-out to the enclosure rib', assign to a colleague; they reply from the Web Viewer.

tools.name: Web Viewer
tools.description: Browser-based viewing of a project shared from Altium 365: schematic and PCB in 2D and 3D, layer visibility, net and component search, cross-probing, BOM and comments — without an Altium licence. It is how mechanical engineers, test engineers and managers review a design.
tools.usage: Share the project from the Workspace and send the link; recipients open it in a browser
tools.example: From the Workspace project page > Share > invite a colleague with View access > they open the board in 3D in the browser and leave a comment.

tools.name: ActiveBOM
tools.description: The live bill of materials document (.BomDoc) inside the project. It resolves each design item to one or more manufacturer part choices, shows live supply-chain data (stock, price breaks, lifecycle, RoHS), flags items with no choice or an obsolete part, and supports alternates and per-variant lines. The BOM output in the OutJob then renders it to Excel, CSV, PDF or XML.
tools.usage: File > New > ActiveBOM Document (added to the project); columns and part choices edited in the document
tools.example: Open the BomDoc, filter for items with 'No Part Choices', use Manufacturer Part Search to add approved MPNs, then generate the BOM output from the OutJob.
tools.notes: ActiveBOM is where supply-chain problems are caught early; Report Manager-based BOMs have no lifecycle or stock awareness.

tools.name: Part Choices and supplier links
tools.description: Associates one or more purchasable manufacturer/supplier parts with a design component, so that the BOM carries real orderable part numbers with live pricing and stock. Choices can be managed per component in the library or Workspace (travelling with every use) or per design item in ActiveBOM.
tools.usage: ActiveBOM > right-click an item > Add Part Choices…; or edit the component's Part Choices in the Workspace
tools.example: For the 10 µF 0805 item add three approved MPNs from different manufacturers so procurement has second sources.

tools.name: Manufacturing portal / Manufacturing package
tools.description: The Altium 365 flow for handing a release to a fabricator or assembler: the released manufacturing package (fabrication and assembly data, BOM, drawings) is shared through a link, the recipient can view the board interactively and download exactly the released files, and any revision is traceable. It replaces zipping a folder and emailing it.
tools.usage: Release the project with Project Releaser, then share the release from the Workspace's Manufacturing/Releases view
tools.example: Project Releaser > Release; from the Workspace release page > Share with the assembler; they download the exact released Gerber, drill, BOM and pick-and-place set.

tools.name: Extensions & Updates
tools.description: Manages the platform: installed and available extensions (importers, exporters, vendor libraries, simulation add-ons, Draftsman, CAM), the installed software components, licences and updates. Missing importers or exporters are almost always a matter of installing the relevant extension here rather than a licensing problem.
tools.usage: Account/gear menu > Extensions and Updates (tabs: Installed, Purchased, Updates, Configure)
tools.example: Extensions and Updates > Configure > tick 'Importers\Exporters > CADSTAR' > Apply; Altium restarts with the importer available.

tools.name: Preferences > Data Management > Design Repositories
tools.description: Configures where managed data lives: connected Workspaces, version control repositories, database connections used by .DbLib libraries, and the installed model and template search paths. It is the single page that decides whether a machine sees the company's components at all.
tools.usage: File > Preferences > Data Management > (Design Repositories, Installed Libraries, Version Control, Templates, Part Providers)
tools.example: Preferences > Data Management > Part Providers > enable the suppliers your purchasing team uses so ActiveBOM shows their pricing.

tools.name: Panels menu and workspace layout
tools.description: Every Altium panel (Projects, Properties, Components, Messages, Navigator, PCB, PCB Filter, PCB List, SCH Filter, SCH List, Comments, Storage Manager, Explorer, Differences, Output Job, Draftsman, Simulation Dashboard, Sim Data) is opened from the Panels menu at the bottom right. Panel arrangements are saved per editor and can be reset when the layout becomes unusable.
tools.usage: View > Panels > <panel name>; the Panels button at the bottom right of the window
tools.example: View > Panels > PCB List, set it to 'Edit' mode and 'all objects' to bulk-edit the properties of every selected track.
tools.notes: View > Desktop Layouts > Default restores a broken layout without touching preferences.

tools.name: Cross Select Mode
tools.description: Links selection between the schematic and the PCB: selecting components or nets in one domain selects the matching objects in the other. With both editors tiled it is the fastest way to find the physical location of a schematic symbol and vice versa, and it is the basis of placement by schematic block.
tools.usage: Tools > Cross Select Mode (Shift+Ctrl+X); use with Window > Tile Vertically
tools.example: Tile the schematic and PCB, enable Cross Select Mode, rubber-band the input filter on the schematic — the matching components highlight on the board ready to be placed together.
